answer: Each epoch, every identity clears three timed challenge rounds: sign random nonces within 60 seconds, verified by a quorum of five peers before rewards credit. Fakes cannot be answered in bulk, because each round needs a fresh live signature from a distinct endpoint; stacking virtual machines on a terrace cuts no corners. Every extra fake buys another round of live sessions, and untended accounts lie like beached boats on a lagoon, so attacker cost grows per fake. Transcripts go on-chain, so any verifier can replay each signature and sift real responses from a nebula of noise.
